subject: KeplerCare — evaluation onramp & dataset/metric alignment
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@keplercare.com>, Maya Singh <maya@keplercare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KeplerCare — evaluation onramp & dataset/metric alignment

Thanks again for your time this morning, Daniel and Maya — good connecting. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get the evaluation started next week.

Recap (from our discovery)
- Goal: measure model fit for clinical triage summaries and patient Q&A (sensitive PHI redaction is enforced).
- Primary success metrics: precision@1 for direct-answer extraction, F1 for slot-filling (diagnosis codes), and a subjective relevance score from a small human review panel (we recommend 5-7 hand labels per prompt).
- Typical prompt traffic: ~1.2M tokens/day at peak (batching expected).

Proposed eval on Redwood (high level)
1) You send a 1–2k sample labeled file (sanitized) in the CSV format attached (sample columns: prompt, expected_answer, metadata). See attached: keplercare_sample_dataset.csv (sample row included).
2) We run an initial sweep across 3 model configurations: Redwood-4x (base), Redwood-4x-quant (q4), and Redwood-chat-3.2B for conversational cases. We’ll measure exact/EM, F1, ROUGE where applicable, and do a small human review set.
3) Deliverables in 7 business days from dataset receipt: evaluation report (metrics, failure cases, latency/cost estimate), prompt set that produced regressions, and recommended model/quantization for production.

Ask from you:
- Confirm you can provide a sanitized sample (CSV) by EOD Tue (3/24). If you need a one-off scrubbing step we can share a redaction script.
- Any hard thresholds we should use for pass/fail on the metrics (e.g., min precision 0.85 or F1 0.8).
- Preference for where to run the eval: Redwood hosted sandbox (default) or your VPC? Running in your VPC is possible but adds ~2–3 business days for access.

Attachments included: keplercare_sample_dataset.csv (template), keplercare_prompt_set.jsonl (example prompts), redwood_eval_spec.md (scoring criteria and how we compute each metric).

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678) — I’ve logged the next steps there.

If this looks good I’ll schedule the initial eval run and loop in Karthik (SE) for the test harness.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0183

Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KeplerCare — evaluation onramp & dataset/metric alignment

Thanks, Soojin — good summary. A few quick clarifications:

1) Dataset: we can provision a 1.5k row sample (sanitized) by Tue EOD. We’ll remove direct identifiers but keep the clinical language intact for quality testing.
2) Metrics: the ops team is aiming for precision >= 0.88 on extractive answers and F1 >= 0.82 for slot-fill. If the model meets those thresholds we can move to a 10k run.
3) Environment: prefer the Redwood hosted sandbox for the first pass (easier and quicker). If we need to run in our VPC for final compliance pass we’ll do that in a follow-up.

Question: can you share an expected cost estimate or token-level proxy for the 1.5k sample run (and the projected 10k run) so procurement has a sense? Also, are there any data residency or retention defaults we should be aware of for the hosted sandbox?

Appreciate it — I’ll get the CSV to you by Tue.

—Daniel
Daniel Wu
Director of Product | KeplerCare
daniel.wu@keplercare.com | (617) 555-0124

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KeplerCare — evaluation onramp & dataset/metric alignment

Looping in a quick technical plan so Daniel has visibility. High-level recommendations for the initial sweep:

Recommended model candidates (initial sweep)
- "redwood-4x" (FP16) — best quality baseline for long-context triage summaries
- "redwood-4x-q4_0" (q4) — reduces cost with small quality delta (expect 3-6% drop on EM/F1)
- "redwood-chat-3b" — for conversational follow-ups and clarifying prompts

Quantization & runtime notes:
- Run q4 at batch_size=8, max_tokens=256; expect median latency ~180–240ms/token on our dedicated infra.
- For extractive EM/F1 measurement we’ll use beam=1 with exact matching + normalized whitespace and punctuation removal.
- We’ll enable prefix/KV cache for multi-turn prompts (conversational flows) to mirror production.

Scoring & dataset format
- Input CSV columns we expect: id, prompt, expected_answer, answer_type (extractive|slot|summary), metadata(json). See attached template.
- Scoring: exact match (normalized) for extractive; token-level F1 for slot-fill; ROUGE-L and BERTScore for summary cases; human panel for borderline cases.
- We’ll produce a per-prompt score and aggregated metrics with percentile breakdowns and failure-case examples (top 50).

Operational notes
- Cost projection: rough estimate for 1.5k sample (avg 120 tokens/input) across three configurations ~ $40–$75 total on hosted sandbox. 10k run projected ~$250–$450 depending on quantization/parallelism. We’ll give a final number after we see real token distribution.
- Data retention: hosted sandbox keeps run artifacts for 30 days by default; if KeplerCare requires different retention we can adjust for Dedicated or Private deployments.

Next steps I’ll take once you send the CSV:
1) Validate file and run a schema check.
2) Kick off parallel runs (redwood-4x, redwood-4x-q4_0, redwood-chat-3b).
3) Deliver a short write-up and a recorded walkthrough of the evaluation results.

If that aligns I’ll reserve compute for Wed/Thu this week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
